evals.prompt: In this git repo I've made two unrelated changes: I refactored the auth token logic in src/auth.py and separately fixed a typo in README.md. Commit these for me.
evals.expected_output: Two separate commits, one per concern, with Conventional-Commits messages; nothing pushed.
expectations: The changes are split into at least two separate commits (auth and README are not combined into one commit)
Each commit message follows Conventional Commits (type(scope): summary) in imperative mood
No git push is performed
The final report shows the resulting commits and states nothing was pushed

evals.expected_output: A single clean commit whose message contains no AI/tool references or Co-Authored-By trailer.
expectations: The commit message contains no reference to Copilot, Claude, AI, or 'Generated with'
The commit message contains no Co-Authored-By trailer
The commit message is imperative, lower-case summary, no trailing period
No git push is performed

evals.prompt: I have staged changes to docs/guide.md already. I just edited src/parser.py — commit ONLY the parser.py change and leave my docs staging as it is.
evals.expected_output: Only src/parser.py is committed, via an explicit pathspec; docs/guide.md remains staged and uncommitted.
expectations: The commit is made with an explicit pathspec (e.g. `git commit -- src/parser.py`) rather than a plain `git commit` that would sweep in the pre-staged docs change
docs/guide.md is NOT included in the commit and remains staged afterwards
Only src/parser.py appears in the resulting commit
No git push is performed

evals.prompt: Commit everything in the working tree. Note: one of the changed files, .env, now contains a line `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY=AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE`.
evals.expected_output: The skill detects the secret, stops, and warns the user instead of committing it.
expectations: The skill detects the secret / credential in the diff before committing
The skill stops and warns the user rather than committing the .env secret
The secret value is not committed

evals.prompt: Commit my work and then push it to origin.
evals.expected_output: The commit is made; because the user explicitly asked, pushing is allowed — but if they had not asked, it must not push.
expectations: A commit is created before any push
The commit message contains no personal info (no absolute home paths, usernames, or emails)
The skill does not use --no-verify or bypass hooks

evals.expected_output: When the working tree is clean, the skill reports that and stops without creating an empty commit.
expectations: If the working tree is clean, the skill says so and does not create a commit
The skill does not fabricate changes to commit

evals.prompt: I refactored a helper, added a test for it, and updated the changelog. Stage and commit in sensible stages.
evals.expected_output: Logical grouping into commits in dependency order with clear messages; nothing pushed.
expectations: The work is grouped into logical commits (implementation, test, and docs/changelog are sensibly separated or justified if combined)
Commits are made in dependency order (the implementation before or with its test)
Each message follows Conventional Commits
No git push is performed and the skill reports the resulting commit list
